name: Algal Bloom
desc: Filamentous green algae blooming and crashing in a lit water column — unbranched Spirogyra threads elongate by intercalary division with helical chloroplast ribbons winding inside their sheaths, trapped oxygen rafts the tangled mats toward the surface, then the nutrients run out, the filaments go yellow, fragment and sink as detritus that remineralises and starts the whole cycle again.

energy.doc: current/stir amplitude + how fast the bloom-crash cycle runs

density.doc: size of the filament population at full bloom (4 at 0 -> 40 at 1)

scale.doc: magnification — 0.35 is a wide low-power field, 2.2 is oil immersion

hue.doc: healthy chloroplast hue (starvation always drifts it toward yellow)

y.doc: field centre down the water column

tangle.doc: how hard the shear tangles the filaments — straight threads at 0, a matted raft at 1

style.doc: aesthetic — wet bright-field on a lit column; additive dark-field where only the specimen glows; Atkins algae photogram on Prussian blue; sumi tonal wash on paper

seed.doc: seeds filament placement, depth planes, helix handedness and buoyancy

alpha.doc: opacity of the algae over the water column
